top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock to Katori and Ye is a mature, independently reproduced achievement: magic-wavelength trapping of many atoms opened a new regime of frequency measurement at the 10^-18 level, now verified across several laboratories and used for redshift tests and constraints on drifting constants and dark matter. The two-name allocation is clean and the citation scope does not overlap the 2005 comb prize, so I prefer awarding it to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; my work is in superconducting circuits, not atomic clocks
